title: Unpopular opinion: you don't need to ask ChatGPT everything
description:
This might be an unpopular opinion, but most people don't need to use cloud AI models for everything.

Most people are using the most state-of-the-art AI models from ChatGPT or Claude to summarize documents or write emails for them, and frankly these models have gotten too smart for that. You don't need all the compute for everyday tasks. 

Running local models directly on your computer means you don't need the internet, your data is completely private, and you're not at the whims of the big AI labs. 

With amazing new local models and even better hardware, your computer can handle 90% of the simple things we ask AI to do.

Would you switch to using a local AI model?

#ai #ainews #NVIDIA #chatGPT #claude

top_reply.author: @Z-Z-W_origin
top_reply.text:
This is outdated before it even reaches production. 
Planar architecture, including interim 2.5D solutions like the Spark, will inevitably become obsolete as monolithic 3D chip architecture takes over. While vertical stacking creates an intense thermal density bottleneck, the industry will overcome this through advanced, non-electrical engineering solutions by embedding lateral microfluidic cooling channels directly between the logic gates and adopting low-temperature fabrication methods. Once these integrated, passive cooling and manufacturing hurdles are resolved, the exponential reduction in vertical wire length and data latency will make investing in 2.5D integration akin to buying an expensive mechanical hard drive right before NVMe SSDs hit the market. 😅
